entries.description: Register.

**Add `evidencePaths` to the finding contract.** A list of repo-relative paths, **required on any finding whose severity is Critical or Major**, on **both** surfaces: the markdown parse in `ai_router/verification.py` and the structured `submit_verdict` tool schema in `ai_router/pull_verifier.py` (today `{description, severity, category}`, `required: ["description"]`). Update the reviewer templates so verifiers are asked for it. A blocking finding with no paths is **unknown**, and unknown still blocks — the anti-laundering default is unchanged.

**Operator decision, journaled — this is the hard carve-out.** Capping any finding's severity is a **verification reduction**; `decision_journal.py` refuses it under AI authority. Present the evidence (Set 116 S3's four rounds; 520 of 572 findings Major) and record the attestation with `authority="human"`, `rubric_line="verification-reduction"`, `verification_effect="reduces"` and a non-empty operator attestation. **No cap is implemented before this record exists.**

**Implement the cap at the one shared chokepoint.** In `is_blocking_issue` / `classify_blocking` — the surface-agnostic predicate both surfaces already consult — a finding whose `evidencePaths` are **all** documentation records at Minor and does not open a round. Ship the falsifiers `L-112-1` requires: one planting a doc-only finding and asserting it does **not** open a round, one planting a mixed doc-and-code finding and asserting it **does**.
Full pytest at close after freeze; verify, close.

Journaled to decisions.jsonl with authority=human, rubric_line=verification-reduction, verification_effect=reduces, three options with consequences, the Set 116 S3 / 520-of-572 evidence, and the reversal path.
Implementing the doc-only cap in is_blocking_issue with the two L-112-1 falsifiers.

Doc-only cap implemented in is_blocking_issue (the one shared chokepoint) via is_doc_only_issue/is_documentation_path; classify_blocking gains doc_capped_issues + names the count in reason. 30 test functions in test_doc_only_cap.py (exactly the spec cap) including the L-112-1 falsifier pairs. TEMPLATE_ID bumped v7->v8 with a new pinned hash (the template edit is a deliberate revision, per the verification-integrity protocol). Workflow doc rule 2a and the router CHANGELOG record it. Discovery verification (K=2, lenses spec-conformance + failure-scenario) returned VERIFIED on round 1 from a cross-provider verifier (gpt-5.5 vs anthropic orchestrator), 0 blocking findings, 2 Minor nits recorded and adjudicated in disposition.json. Disposition authored and validated.
Register.

**Build `python -m ai_router.close_preflight`.** Runnable at any time against a session set and session number, with **no side effects and no routed call**. It evaluates the same predicates the close evaluates, by calling them rather than re-implementing them, and prints every unmet obligation in one pass, each with the command or action that satisfies it. Exit non-zero when anything blocking is unmet.

**Cover the expensive case.** The preflight must answer *"would the verification backstop fire?"* — does a stamped round exist for this session — **without** spending the round. That one line is 78 of the **148 still-blocking** historical failures (the other 64 of the 212 belong to checks Set 116 S3 demoted, so pre-empting those is worth nothing now).

**Prove it against history.** Replay the preflight's predicates over the recorded failures in `session-events.jsonl` and report how many it would have pre-empted. The ~148-of-212 figure in this spec is a **prediction derived from a one-off query, not from an instrument.** The session records the measured number, and a discrepancy is a finding — **about the tool *or* about this spec's prediction, and the session must say which.**
Full pytest at close after freeze; verify, close.

Register. Preload read (constitution, project-guidance, lessons-learned, AGENTS.md); transport profile copilot-cli confirmed via ai_router/local-overrides.yaml (no provider keys by design); start_session run for session 2; session-start checklist posted; no decision-review-queue.jsonl entries to triage.

Built ai_router/close_preflight.py: evaluate() walks gate_checks.GATE_CHECKS by CALLING each predicate the close calls (plus the synthetic disposition_present row, reported alongside the chain rather than short-circuiting it as run_gate_checks does), tags each row blocking/advisory from is_blocking_check, and prints every unmet obligation in one pass with the predicate remediation verbatim plus a canonical action. No lock, no events, no writes, no routed call. Exit 1 when anything blocking is unmet, 0 otherwise, 2 on invalid invocation. Reports only; adds no gate.

Covered the 79-of-214 verification_backstop case without spending the round. Extracted close_backstop.decide_backstop() (+ BackstopDecision) out of run_close_backstop, which now consumes it, so the preflight predicts the backstop by calling the same sequence instead of copying it. Every branch of that sequence is a pure read (method token, budget.yaml, orchestrator identity, stamped rows and their hash-bound artifacts, round ledger, git diff base). Three answers: will not run (met), will refuse before routing (unmet+blocking, backstop remediation verbatim), will route (met + COST WARNING, never a refusal -- a backstop round returning VERIFIED closes fine, and inventing a refusal would make this a gate). Only EvidenceTooLargeError stays unpredicted; it is raised by the assembly after the decision.

Shipped the replay as an instrument (--replay-history), not a one-off query, and measured it: 186 closeout_failed events, 214 recorded check-failures, 64 belonging to checks Set 116 S3 demoted, 150 still blocking today, and the preflight covers 150 of 150. VERDICT ON THE DISCREPANCY: the spec PREDICTION WAS RIGHT and the corpus grew. Filtering the ledger to before 2026-08-10T20:28Z reproduces the spec digit for digit -- 184 events, 212 check-failures, 148 still-blocking, 78 verification_backstop, 122 sessions. The delta is exactly Set 117 Session 1 close-out failures (verification_backstop at 20:28:56Z, test_run_fresh at 20:29:47Z), recorded after the spec was authored. One real instrument defect was found and fixed in the same pass: session_number 0 in a legacy Set 047 event was being counted as a session, inflating the session tally by one (123 vs 122); non-positive session numbers are now excluded from the session tally while their check-failures still count, with a falsifier test.

Verification: 5 rounds (2 discovery + 2 remediation-review + 1 operator-authorized). 8 findings, all accepted, none disputed. Round 5 returned VERIFIED with 8/8 fix verdicts accepted and zero findings. Root causes fixed: (1) evaluate() now mirrors close_session ordering -- backstop decision FIRST, then the gate chain with extra_clean_ignore from the settling row, and verification_integrity reported as not-yet-decidable when the backstop would route; (2) --session-number is an assertion that is checked, not a partial override; (3) the two set-terminal policy gates are reported, mirroring the close TTY posture; (4) the verdict is a tri-state so the JSON and human surfaces cannot disagree. Full pytest on the frozen tree: 3975 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed in 617.04s (10:17), recorded as the pytest run of record (digest e565fea2f7cf).
Register.

**Stop the backstop firing when nothing changed.** Session 2's own close proved this live: `cite_lessons` — *mandated at close* — bumped three `last-used-set` trailers after a VERIFIED round-5 stamp, staling it. Source, tests and docs were byte-identical; only metadata moved, and the close needed `--manual-verify` to complete. `WORK_DIFF_BASE_EXCLUDES` already carries `s*-rounds.jsonl`, `checklist-posts.jsonl` and `test-runs.jsonl` — **all three inside `docs/session-sets/<slug>/`.** The mechanism has an implicit *per-set* scope and no concept of a close-mandated write outside it; `cite_lessons` writes `LESSONS_ACTIVE` **and** `LESSONS_ARCHIVE`, both repo-wide. Fix it as a **category — the artifacts the close-out procedure is itself required to write — not as a fourth list entry.** The acceptance test is not "does `lessons-learned.md` stop staling"; it is *would a fifth close-mandated writer, in either scope, be excluded without editing a list?* Ship the falsifier `L-112-1` requires: a passed round plus a `cite_lessons` write must settle the close with **zero** fresh metered rounds.

**Make the recovery path reachable, and its failures survivable.** Three parts, one surface. **(a)** A backstop round writes a `discoveryBaselineTree` alongside the ledger row Set 116 S2 appends, so `--phase remediation-review` is reachable instead of refusing with `EXIT_USAGE` (`verify_session.py:2945-2954`). Cover the case the current behaviour ignores: a **clean** discovery round writes no envelope, so it leaves no baseline either. **(b)** `close_backstop`'s blocking text names `verify_session` as the sanctioned next step; after (a) that instruction must actually work, and the message should name the phase. A test asserts the named command succeeds from the exact state the message is printed in. **(c)** `EvidenceTooLargeError` and `VerifySessionError` are **siblings** (`verify_session.py:449,453`), and `close_backstop` catches the latter at four sites (311, 635, 808, 827) but the former at **one** (779) — so an oversized bundle still crashes the close with an unhandled traceback on four paths, taking the gate down with no remediation line. One line fixes all four: make `EvidenceTooLargeError` inherit from `VerifySessionError`. **Check the catch ordering at 779 first** — a subclass caught after its parent is unreachable.

**Delete what nothing reaches.** Two groups, same proof obligation. **(a) The unreachable gate machinery:** `contract_gate.py`, `floor_ratchet.py`, `replacement_gate.py`, `spec_admission.py`, `routed_gate.py` and their tests (**3,285 LOC, ~220 tests**). **(b) The cost surface that a Copilot seat cannot populate:** `pricing_proposal.py` and `cost_report.py` and their tests (**1,880 LOC, ~150 tests**) — across 83 routed calls every metrics row carries `billed_usage_unavailable: true` and `cost_usd: 0.0`. **`pricing.py` STAYS** — `models.py`, `pull_verifier.py`, `config.py` and `__init__.py` import it, and it feeds the api-profile verifier's `max_cost_multiplier` guard; deleting it breaks the Direct API path. Prove unreachability first for every module: no import from any close path, no console-script entry point, no reference in `router-config.yaml`. A module that turns out to be reachable **stays and is reported**, not forced.
Full pytest at close after freeze; verify, close.

Register. Preload read (constitution, project-guidance, lessons-learned, AGENTS.md); transport profile copilot-cli confirmed via local-overrides.yaml (no provider keys by design); start_session registered session 3/3; session-start checklist posted; decision-review-queue.jsonl absent (nothing to triage).

Fixed the close-mandated-write staleness as a CATEGORY: writers declare a module-level CLOSE_MANDATED_WRITES literal and verification_stamp DISCOVERS them by ast (no import, no side effects, safe on the close path), so a fifth writer in either scope is exempt with nothing here to edit. Two bounds, because the honesty matters: a per-set ledger is close output end-to-end (whole-file), while a guidance file is only PARTLY mandated -- cite_lessons owns one trailer field and the lesson prose around it is session work. So cite_lessons declares a normalizer (guidance_meta.normalize_close_mandated_metadata) and the digest compares normalized-current against normalized-at-base, dropping the file entirely when only the mandated field moved. A wholesale exemption would have let a post-verification rewrite of a PRELOAD document ride a passed round -- a verification reduction, and not one this set is authorized to make. Falsifiers (L-112-1), 32 in ai_router/tests/test_close_mandated_writes.py: planted cite_lessons bump -> digest unchanged AND validate_stamped_row still ok (zero fresh metered rounds); planted look-alike prose edit -> digest moves AND the row goes stale with the work-changed reason; synthetic fifth writer in a throwaway package tree, both scopes and both bounds; malformed/non-literal declarations fail closed.

Three parts, one surface. (a) The baseline record moved to where every round writes: record_round_completed gains discovery_baseline_tree (omit-null) and find_discovery_baseline_tree reads the ledger as well as the envelopes. The envelope is written only on findings-bearing rounds, so the two states that most need a baseline left none -- a CLEAN discovery round and every close-backstop round (unphased) -- and --phase remediation-review refused with EXIT_USAGE. verify_session now snapshots for every round except remediation-review itself (which must never become a baseline, or a second cycle would diff from the first fix), and close_backstop snapshots before it writes anything. (b) _verify_session_command takes an optional phase; the backstop's blocking remediation now names --phase remediation-review, which is honest only because (a) made it work. (c) EvidenceTooLargeError now INHERITS VerifySessionError. It was a sibling caught at one of five sites, so an oversized bundle crashed the close with a traceback on four paths; fixing the type fixes all four (L-069-1, the class not the instance). The exit-code split never lived in the class relationship, only in handler ORDER -- and the CLI caught the parent FIRST, so the reorder at verify_session.py was mandatory: a subclass caught after its parent is unreachable code. 10 falsifiers appended to test_close_backstop.py, including the spec's: the refusal message is PARSED, not paraphrased, and the command it names is executed from the exact state it was printed in (round 2 resolves the baseline and returns EXIT_OK).

Proved reachability FIRST with a static import graph over all 78 ai_router modules (ast, no execution), then applied the spec's own escape clause. THE SPEC'S LIST WAS WRONG ABOUT THREE OF SEVEN, and they stay and are reported: contract_gate (close_session.run calls validate_contract_gate as a live close gate; close_preflight and start_session call it too -- it is ON the close path the spec says it is off), spec_admission (session_checklist.read_spec_steps calls parse_session_plans to seed the plan the checklist_posted gate reads), replacement_gate (dual_surface_verify imports validate_benchmark_registration at module scope and calls it -- deleting it would break that module outright, and editing a survivor to manufacture unreachability is exactly the forcing the spec forbids). DELETED, all four proven unreachable: floor_ratchet (914), routed_gate (437), pricing_proposal (1581), cost_report (551) = 3,483 LOC plus 3,012 lines of tests (235 tests). The line drawn and journaled: a module is reachable when a SURVIVING module CALLS it; an __init__ re-export is publication, not use. pricing.py STAYS as the spec requires. Every echo fixed in one pass (L-065-1): __init__ re-exports and docstring, config.py and pricing.py operator messages that named a deleted command, the routed_gate config block and the dead cost_report_on_exit key, four test modules, and the doc instructions in ai-led-session-workflow.md, close-out.md, pull-verifier.md, repository-reference.md and verification-surface-strategy.md.

Full pytest on the frozen tree: 3,780 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed in 513.23s, recorded as the run of record (digest 859283c79f4f). The FIRST full run failed one test and it was a real finding, not a flake: the first cut of the baseline change widened the Set 096 ENVELOPE contract when only the round LEDGER needed it. Narrowed the change, re-ran the suite in full so the run of record postdates the last code change. Dogfooded close_preflight before verifying (it named working_tree_clean and the backstop cost correctly). Verification: one --phase discovery round, 2-call fan-out (spec-conformance + failure-scenario), both gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded by registry lookup on claude-opus-5 -- VERIFIED, zero findings, zero nits. Authored s3-conventions.md up front per L-064-10, plus change-log.md (set-terminal), the disposition and the ai-assignment close-out block.
